subject: re-calculating needed for Hildebrand if 30 Hz used as sampling rate?

messages.author: 75c27e2c724c8096
messages.subject: re-calculating needed for Hildebrand if 30 Hz used as sampling rate?
parts:
Hi 

i have a quick question. I have collected my Actigraph data with childeren at a sampling rate of 30 hz. 
Now I want to apply the Hildebrand cut-points actigraph hip worn. Should i do any re-calculations as these cut-points were established using 60 hz sampling rate? And if yes, how should i do this?


many many thanks for your response
Manon

messages.author: 017566be30afa7f3
messages.subject: Re: [GGIR] re-calculating needed for Hildebrand if 30 Hz used as sampling rate?
parts:
Hi Manon,

No correction is needed because metrics like ENMO look at the mean magnitude of the signal, rather than area under the curve or that kind of metrics. So, if we assume the shape of the signal is identical except for the resolution of the data points than mean should be the same.

For other cut-points published in literature this may not be true and you would need to adjust the cut-point accordingly as explained in our vignette: https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/GGIR/vignettes/CutPoints.html

The above is about the (absence of) interaction between sampling rate and the design of the acceleration metric. Aside from that it is possible that the acceleration the sensor itself produces different output at 30 compared with 60 Hertz, although this influence is likely to be small (ongoing research). ... But even if there would be differences it would be very hard to account for it, because you would need to be able to compare the specific sensors used in that study with your own sensors and from that derive some scaling factor.

Vincent
